content: This product information provides details about the medication but does not guarantee its safety, effectiveness, or suitability for your specific needs. It is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your health condition. Uses: This medication is prescribed to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs called cephalosporin antibiotics. It is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, typically once or twice daily. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before taking cefadroxil, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, penicillins, other cephalosporins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Cefadroxil may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), reducing their effectiveness. The liquid suspension may contain sugar, so caution is advised if you have diabetes or other conditions requiring sugar restriction. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may cause false-positive results in certain diabetic urine tests (e.g., cupric sulfate-type) and may affect the results of some lab tests. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Storage: Store capsules or tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Store the liquid suspension in the refrigerator and discard any unused portion after 14 days. Do not freeze. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This summary does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
